_comment: A worked example. Invented, not anyone's prescription — it exists to show every feature of the format in one place: a spacing group, a tapering course, meal-relative dosing and an as-needed medicine.

medicines._comment: Four times across the waking day. Shares a spacing group, so it is never asked for within ten minutes of another drop.
medicines.name: Antibiotic eye drop

medicines._comment: A taper: four times a day for a week, then three times a day for a week. Common for steroids, and impossible to express without phases.
medicines.name: Steroid eye drop

medicines._comment: Two-hourly and ongoing. Note it keeps its own schedule despite sharing the spacing group.
medicines.name: Lubricating eye drop

medicines._comment: Before food actually matters for this one, so it carries an offset.
medicines.name: Stomach protection capsule

medicines._comment: With food, so no offset — inventing a delay would be its own kind of wrong.
medicines.name: Anti-inflammatory tablet

medicines._comment: Never fires on its own. /took records it against the gap and the daily cap.
medicines.name: Painkiller
